task_3.title: Support DataTree comparison in assert_allclose
task_3.description: Prior to this change, xarray's testing.assert_allclose() did not accept DataTree objects, raising a TypeError when users attempted to compare two DataTree instances for approximate equality. This update adds DataTree support to assert_allclose by traversing the full subtree structure of each DataTree and comparing all nodes (coordinate names and variables) using the same allclose semantics already available for Dataset and Variable. Additionally, the internal Dataset._all_compat method was generalized to accept a callable comparator in addition to a method-name string, enabling more flexible compatibility checks.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that testing.assert_allclose() accepts DataTree objects and compares them for approximate equality across their entire tree structure. Previously, passing DataTree instances to assert_allclose() raised a TypeError because the function only handled Variable, DataArray, Dataset, and Coordinates types. Users who work with hierarchical data via DataTree had no built-in assertion utility for approximate comparison in tests.

expectation.grounded: When two DataTree objects are passed to testing.assert_allclose(), the function should traverse the subtree of each DataTree (via subtree_with_keys), compare every corresponding node's coordinate names and variables using the allclose-compatible variable comparator, and raise an AssertionError with a diff_datatree_repr message if any node differs beyond tolerance. The Dataset._all_compat method should accept either a string method name or a callable of type Callable[[Variable, Variable], bool] as its compat parameter, using the callable directly when provided.
expectation.conceptual: When users call assert_allclose with two DataTree objects, the function should recursively compare all nodes in both trees for approximate numerical equality. If corresponding nodes differ beyond the tolerance, an AssertionError should be raised with a human-readable representation of the differences. The comparison should check both structural equality (matching coordinate names and tree paths) and value-level approximate equality across all variables at every node.

constraints.grounded: Existing assert_allclose behavior for Variable, DataArray, Dataset, and Coordinates must remain unchanged. The Dataset._all_compat method must continue to work with string-based compat arguments exactly as before (backward compatible). DataTree comparison must use the same tolerance semantics (rtol, atol) as the existing Variable-level allclose logic. A TypeError must still be raised for unsupported types passed to assert_allclose.
constraints.conceptual: The addition of DataTree support must not alter the behavior of assert_allclose for any previously supported types. All existing tests and usage patterns must continue to work identically. The tolerance handling for DataTree comparisons must be consistent with how tolerances are applied for other supported types.

behavior: testing.assert_allclose() now accepts DataTree instances as both arguments without raising TypeError
When two DataTree objects are compared, all nodes across the full subtree hierarchy are checked for approximate equality
Each node comparison verifies that coordinate names match and that all variables are allclose-equivalent
When a mismatch is found between DataTree nodes, an AssertionError is raised with a DataTree-specific diff representation
Dataset._all_compat now accepts a callable comparator directly in addition to the previous string-based method name interface
When _all_compat receives a string, it resolves it to a method via getattr as before; when it receives a callable, it uses it directly
acceptance_criteria: When two identical DataTree objects are passed to assert_allclose(), the assertion passes without error
When two DataTree objects with values differing within the specified tolerance are passed to assert_allclose(), the assertion passes
When two DataTree objects with values differing beyond the specified tolerance are passed to assert_allclose(), an AssertionError is raised
When the raised AssertionError message for mismatched DataTree objects contains a human-readable diff representation of the tree differences
When a DataTree with nested subtree nodes is compared, all levels of the hierarchy are checked, not just the root node
When two DataTree objects have different coordinate names at any node, the assertion fails even if variable values are close
When two DataTree objects have different tree structures (mismatched paths/keys), the assertion fails
When assert_allclose() is called with Variable, DataArray, Dataset, or Coordinates, behavior remains unchanged from prior versions
When Dataset._all_compat is called with a string argument, it behaves identically to the previous implementation
When Dataset._all_compat is called with a callable comparator, it uses that callable directly for variable comparison
When an unsupported type is passed to assert_allclose(), a TypeError is still raised

task_4.title: Support chunks='auto' for cftime datasets
task_4.description: Previously, opening a dataset with use_cftime=True and chunks='auto' raised a NotImplementedError from dask because cftime datetimes are stored as object dtype, and dask cannot estimate byte sizes for object arrays. This change makes xarray transparently handle cftime object-dtype variables during auto-chunking by approximating their per-element byte size and rescaling the chunk-size target to an equivalent float64-based limit, allowing normalize_chunks to succeed. The same logic is also applied during rechunk operations on chunked arrays containing cftime data. A new get_auto_chunk_size method is added to the ChunkManagerEntrypoint API so chunk managers can supply their configured target chunk size.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xr.open_dataset (and open_mfdataset) with chunks='auto' succeeds when the dataset contains cftime datetime variables (use_cftime=True or cftime-decoded coordinates). Previously this combination raised a NotImplementedError because dask cannot auto-chunk object-dtype arrays. The fix should also ensure that rechunking an already-chunked array containing cftime datetimes with chunks='auto' works correctly.

expectation.grounded: When xr.open_dataset is called with chunks='auto' and the dataset contains cftime datetime variables, _get_chunk (now in xarray.namedarray.utils) should detect cftime data via _contains_cftime_datetimes, call fake_target_chunksize to compute a rescaled byte-size limit based on float64 itemsize relative to the approximate per-element object size, and pass that limit along with a float64 dtype to ChunkManagerEntrypoint.normalize_chunks. The ChunkManagerEntrypoint.rechunk method should similarly detect cftime data and resolve auto chunks before delegating to the underlying array's rechunk. ChunkManagerEntrypoint gains a get_auto_chunk_size method; DaskManager implements it by reading dask's 'array.chunk-size' config. In-memory variables encountered during _chunk_ds should be skipped rather than passed through the chunking pipeline.
expectation.conceptual: When a user opens or rechunks a dataset that contains cftime datetime coordinates using chunks='auto', the operation should succeed and produce reasonable chunk sizes rather than raising an error. The chunking system should internally estimate the byte size of cftime objects, translate that into an equivalent fixed-dtype chunk target, and let the chunk manager's normalization algorithm determine appropriate chunk boundaries. Chunk managers must be able to report their default auto-chunk size target.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter chunking behavior for non-cftime (fixed-dtype) variables; they must continue to use their original dtype and no rescaled limit. In-memory variables must be preserved as-is during _chunk_ds and not passed into the chunking logic. The existing warning about specified chunks separating stored chunks must still be emitted. The ChunkManagerEntrypoint.get_auto_chunk_size base implementation must raise NotImplementedError with a descriptive message so third-party chunk managers that do not implement it receive clear guidance. fake_target_chunksize must short-circuit and return the original limit and dtype for non-cftime data.
constraints.conceptual: Auto-chunking of standard (non-cftime) datasets must remain completely unaffected. Variables already loaded into memory should not be re-chunked during dataset opening. The chunk manager abstraction must remain extensible, with a clear contract for third-party implementations to supply their auto-chunk size. The byte-size estimation approach must be conservative and not introduce silent data corruption or incorrect chunk boundaries.

behavior: xr.open_dataset with chunks='auto' and cftime datetime variables no longer raises NotImplementedError; it returns a lazily-chunked Dataset with valid chunk sizes.
fake_target_chunksize estimates the per-element byte size of cftime objects by sampling the first element, computes a ratio against float64 itemsize, and rescales the byte-size limit accordingly.
The rescaled limit and a float64 dtype are passed to normalize_chunks in place of the original object dtype, allowing dask's auto_chunks algorithm to proceed.
ChunkManagerEntrypoint.rechunk detects cftime data and resolves auto-chunk specifications via _get_chunk before delegating to the underlying array's rechunk method.
ChunkManagerEntrypoint.get_auto_chunk_size is a new method; the base class raises NotImplementedError, and DaskManager implements it by reading dask config 'array.chunk-size'.
In _chunk_ds, variables that are already in memory (var._in_memory is True) are preserved directly without entering the chunking pipeline.

_get_chunk is relocated from xarray.structure.chunks to xarray.namedarray.utils and now accepts raw duck-array data, preferred_chunks, and dims as explicit parameters instead of receiving a Variable object.
acceptance_criteria: When opening a dataset with xr.open_dataset(path, chunks='auto', use_cftime=True) containing cftime time coordinates, the call succeeds and returns a Dataset with dask-backed arrays having valid chunk sizes.
When opening a dataset with xr.open_dataset(path, chunks='auto') on a standard datetime64 dataset, behavior and chunk sizes are identical to before the change.
When calling .chunk('auto') on a DataArray or Dataset containing cftime datetime data, the rechunk operation succeeds and produces valid chunk sizes.

When a third-party ChunkManagerEntrypoint subclass that does not implement get_auto_chunk_size is used with cftime data and chunks='auto', a NotImplementedError is raised with a message indicating get_auto_chunk_size must be implemented.
When _chunk_ds processes variables that are already in memory, those variables are included in the result unchanged and are not passed through chunk normalization.
When specified chunks conflict with backend-preferred chunks on a cftime dataset, the existing user-level warning about separated stored chunks is still emitted.

task_2.title: Support NETCDF4_CLASSIC format with h5netcdf engine
task_2.description: The h5netcdf backend now accepts format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' when writing NetCDF files via ds.to_netcdf(). This allows users to produce classic-compatible NetCDF4 files without relying on the netcdf4-python library and its C dependencies. When the classic format is selected, variables and attributes are encoded using NetCDF3-compatible types, and sub-group creation is disallowed since the classic data model does not support groups. A minimum h5netcdf version (> 1.6.4) is required for full format support; older versions raise an error. Note that until h5netcdf 1.7.0, the output files are pseudo-classic and may not be recognized as genuine NETCDF4_CLASSIC by all third-party tools.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can write NETCDF4_CLASSIC-format files using the h5netcdf engine by specifying format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' in to_netcdf(), so they can avoid using netcdf4-python (and its C dependencies) while still producing files compatible with applications that only support classic NetCDF4 features. Ensure that variables and attributes are automatically cast to NetCDF3-compatible types. Ensure that attempting to create sub-groups under the classic format raises an appropriate error. Ensure that an informative error is raised when the installed h5netcdf version is too old to support this feature.

expectation.grounded: H5NetCDFStore.open() must accept format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' in addition to 'NETCDF4' and None. When format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', encode_variable() must delegate to encode_nc3_variable instead of _encode_nc4_variable, and set_attribute() must pass attribute values through encode_nc3_attr_value. The format must be forwarded to _get_datatype via the nc_format parameter. get_child_store() must raise ValueError when format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC'. When h5netcdf version is <= 1.6.4 and format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', open() must raise ValueError indicating that h5netcdf >= 1.7.0 is required. When h5netcdf version is > 1.6.4, the format keyword must be passed through to h5netcdf.File. Unsupported format strings must raise ValueError with an informative message.
expectation.conceptual: When a user calls to_netcdf with engine='h5netcdf' and format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC', the library should produce a NetCDF4 file whose variables and attributes are restricted to the classic (NetCDF3-compatible) data model. All variable data and attribute values should be automatically cast to types supported by the classic format. Attempting to create hierarchical groups should be rejected with a clear error. If the installed h5netcdf version does not support native classic format writing, a clear error should inform the user of the version requirement.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior for format='NETCDF4' and format=None must remain unchanged. The default format must remain 'NETCDF4'. The h5netcdf version check must compare against version 1.6.4 using packaging.version.Version. Variable-level attributes written during prepare_variable must also be encoded through encode_nc3_attr_value when in classic mode. No new public API surface beyond accepting 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC' as a format value should be introduced.
constraints.conceptual: Default writing behavior must not change for users who do not specify the classic format. The feature must not alter the content or structure of files written in the standard NETCDF4 format. Version compatibility must be checked at file-open time, not deferred to write time, so users receive immediate feedback. Attribute and variable encoding for classic mode must reuse the existing NetCDF3 encoding logic rather than introducing a separate implementation.

behavior: H5NetCDFStore.open() now accepts 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC' as a valid format parameter value
When format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', global attributes are encoded via encode_nc3_attr_value before being set on the dataset
When format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', variables are encoded via encode_nc3_variable instead of _encode_nc4_variable
When format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', variable-level attributes are also encoded via encode_nc3_attr_value during prepare_variable
When format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', _get_datatype receives nc_format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' to resolve types appropriately
When format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', get_child_store raises ValueError because the classic data model does not support sub-groups
When h5netcdf version is > 1.6.4, the format keyword argument is passed to h5netcdf.File
When h5netcdf version is <= 1.6.4 and format is 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC', a ValueError is raised indicating h5netcdf >= 1.7.0 is required
Format values other than 'NETCDF4' and 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC' raise ValueError with the invalid format name in the message
The H5NetCDFStore constructor now stores the format parameter, defaulting to 'NETCDF4' when None is provided
acceptance_criteria: When calling ds.to_netcdf with engine='h5netcdf' and format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC', the file is written successfully with variables and attributes cast to NetCDF3-compatible types
When calling ds.to_netcdf with engine='h5netcdf' and format='NETCDF4' (or no format), behavior is identical to the previous version
When attempting to write a dataset with groups using format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' and engine='h5netcdf', a ValueError is raised indicating sub-groups are not allowed
When h5netcdf version is <= 1.6.4 and format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' is specified, a ValueError is raised mentioning the h5netcdf >= 1.7.0 requirement
When an unsupported format string (e.g., 'NETCDF3_CLASSIC') is passed to the h5netcdf backend, a ValueError is raised indicating the format is invalid

Given a dataset with attributes containing types not supported by the classic model, when written with format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' and engine='h5netcdf', those attributes are automatically encoded to compatible types
Given a dataset with variables using NetCDF4-only data types, when written with format='NETCDF4_CLASSIC' and engine='h5netcdf', the variables are encoded to NetCDF3-compatible types

task_1.title: Support DataTree objects in xarray.merge() and xarray.concat()
task_1.description: The xarray.merge() and xarray.concat() top-level functions are extended to accept DataTree objects in addition to Dataset and DataArray. When DataTree objects are passed, the functions operate node-by-node across the tree structure and return a DataTree. This enables users to merge or concatenate hierarchical data directly without manually iterating over tree nodes using map_over_datasets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray.concat() and xarray.merge() accept DataTree objects as inputs and return a DataTree result, allowing users to concatenate or merge hierarchical tree-structured data along a specified dimension or across variables without resorting to manual per-node iteration via map_over_datasets.

expectation.grounded: When xarray.concat() is called with an iterable of DataTree objects, it should dispatch to an internal DataTree concatenation path that uses group_subtrees to iterate over corresponding nodes, concatenate the dataset at each node via _dataset_concat, and return a DataTree constructed from the merged results. A new overload on concat() should accept Iterable[DataTree] and return DataTree. The dim parameter type should be broadened to Hashable across concat's internal helpers (_dataset_concat, _dataarray_concat). A preexisting_dim flag should allow _dataset_concat to handle dimensions that exist elsewhere in the tree but not at the current node. When xarray.merge() is called with DataTree objects, it should dispatch to a merge_trees helper that collects nodes by path, merges root datasets first, then processes child nodes level by level using merge_core, and returns a DataTree. A new overload on merge() should accept Iterable[DataTree] and return DataTree. If compat is 'identical' in concat, a ValueError should be raised when tree names differ. If trees are not isomorphic in concat, a ValueError should be raised (wrapping TreeIsomorphismError). If mixed types (DataTree alongside non-DataTree) are passed to merge, a TypeError should be raised. If fill_value is set to a non-default value for DataTree in merge, a NotImplementedError should be raised.
expectation.conceptual: When a user passes DataTree objects to xarray.concat(), the function should concatenate corresponding nodes across all trees along the specified dimension and return a new DataTree preserving the hierarchical structure. When a user passes DataTree objects to xarray.merge(), the function should merge variables at corresponding nodes across all trees and return a new DataTree. Both functions should validate that all inputs are of consistent type and that trees have compatible structures, raising clear errors otherwise. The return type should be DataTree when DataTree inputs are provided, and Dataset otherwise.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior of concat() and merge() for Dataset, DataArray, and dict-like inputs must remain unchanged. The concat() overload resolution must check for DataTree before DataArray to avoid misrouting. The merge() function must reject mixed-type iterables containing both DataTree and non-DataTree objects with a TypeError. The merge_trees helper must raise NotImplementedError when fill_value is not dtypes.NA for DataTree inputs. The concat DataTree path must validate tree isomorphism via group_subtrees and propagate TreeIsomorphismError as ValueError. The dim parameter in _dataset_concat and _dataarray_concat must accept Hashable, not just str.
constraints.conceptual: All pre-existing concatenation and merge behavior for non-tree objects must be preserved as a non-regression requirement. Mixing DataTree with non-DataTree objects in a single merge call is not permitted. Custom fill_value is not yet supported for DataTree merge. Trees must have matching hierarchical structure (isomorphism) to be concatenated. Type overloads must correctly distinguish DataTree inputs from Dataset/DataArray inputs for static type checking.

behavior: xarray.concat() accepts an iterable of DataTree objects and returns a DataTree by concatenating corresponding node datasets along the given dimension.
xarray.merge() accepts an iterable of DataTree objects and returns a DataTree by merging variables at each corresponding node path.
When concat is called with DataTree inputs and compat='identical', it raises ValueError if the tree names are not identical across all inputs.
When concat is called with non-isomorphic DataTree objects, it raises ValueError indicating all trees must be isomorphic.
When merge is called with a mix of DataTree and non-DataTree objects, it raises TypeError.
When merge is called with DataTree objects and a non-default fill_value, it raises NotImplementedError.
Concat handles pre-existing dimensions that appear in some tree nodes but not others by marking the dimension as pre-existing for _dataset_concat.
The dim parameter for internal concat helpers now accepts any Hashable, not just str.
New type overloads ensure static type checkers correctly infer DataTree return types when DataTree inputs are provided.
merge_trees processes child nodes level by level (sorted by tree depth) and merges inherited indexes to ensure alignment.
acceptance_criteria: When xarray.concat() is called with a list of DataTree objects sharing the same structure and a valid dimension, it should return a DataTree with concatenated data at each corresponding node.
When xarray.merge() is called with a list of DataTree objects, it should return a DataTree with merged variables at each node path.
When xarray.concat() is called with DataTree objects that have differing tree structures (non-isomorphic), it should raise a ValueError.
When xarray.concat() is called with DataTree objects, compat='identical', and differing root names, it should raise a ValueError about non-identical names.
When xarray.merge() is called with a mix of DataTree and Dataset objects, it should raise a TypeError.
When xarray.merge() is called with DataTree objects and a custom fill_value (not NA), it should raise a NotImplementedError.
When xarray.concat() or xarray.merge() is called with Dataset or DataArray inputs (no DataTree), existing behavior should be unchanged.
When xarray.concat() is called with DataTree objects along a dimension that exists only in some nodes, it should correctly handle the pre-existing dimension without errors.
Static type checkers should infer a DataTree return type when DataTree inputs are passed to concat() or merge(), and Dataset return type for Dataset/DataArray inputs.

task_5.title: Preserve attributes by default across all xarray operations
task_5.description: The default behavior of attribute preservation in xarray has changed from dropping attributes to preserving them across all operations. Previously, operations such as reductions, binary arithmetic, groupby, rolling, resampling, missing-data handling, indexing, and apply_ufunc would discard attrs unless the user explicitly passed keep_attrs=True or set xr.set_options(keep_attrs=True). Starting in 2025.11.0, the default for keep_attrs is True, so attributes flow through all operations automatically. Additionally, binary operations between two xarray objects now combine attributes from both operands using a drop_conflicts merge strategy (keeping attributes whose values match, dropping those that conflict) instead of the former behavior of retaining only the left operand's attributes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that all xarray operations (reductions, binary arithmetic, comparisons, groupby, rolling, resampling, weighted, apply_ufunc, where, isnull, notnull, map, and data-manipulation methods) preserve attributes by default when keep_attrs is not explicitly specified. Ensure that binary operations between two xarray objects combine attributes from both operands using a drop_conflicts strategy, keeping matching attribute key-value pairs and discarding conflicting ones. Ensure that users can restore the previous attribute-dropping behavior globally via xr.set_options(keep_attrs=False), per-operation via keep_attrs=False, or via context manager.

expectation.grounded: When keep_attrs is None (not explicitly provided), _get_keep_attrs must resolve to True across Dataset.reduce, Dataset.map, Dataset._binary_op, Dataset.fillna, Dataset.where (the method), Variable.reduce, Variable.quantile, Variable.isnull, Variable.notnull, Variable._binary_op, Variable.coarsen_reshape, DatasetView.map, DataWithCoords.isnull, DataWithCoords.notnull, the top-level xr.where function, and apply_ufunc. For binary operations on Variable and Dataset, when keep_attrs is active, merge_attrs must be called with the drop_conflicts combine_attrs strategy on attributes from both operands. Dataset.map must convert non-DataArray return values to DataArray before proceeding, and when keep_attrs is False it must explicitly clear attrs on all result variables and coordinates.
expectation.conceptual: All xarray operations should preserve attributes by default. Users who do not pass an explicit keep_attrs argument should see attributes carried through reductions, transformations, binary operations, missing-data methods, and ufunc applications. Binary operations between two attributed objects should merge their attributes, keeping entries that agree and dropping entries that conflict. The previous default of discarding attributes should remain accessible via an explicit opt-out.

constraints.grounded: Explicitly passing keep_attrs=False to any operation must still drop attributes, yielding empty attrs or None as before. xr.set_options(keep_attrs=False) must globally restore the old attribute-dropping default. Binary operations with a scalar operand (which has no attrs) must preserve the xarray object's attributes unchanged. The drop_conflicts merge strategy must be order-independent: (a op b).attrs must equal (b op a).attrs for commutative operations. DataArray.reduce docstrings must document the new default as True.
constraints.conceptual: The opt-out mechanism for dropping attributes must remain fully functional. Global and per-call overrides must behave identically to how they worked before, only the default changes. Attribute merging in binary operations must be symmetric and must not silently discard non-conflicting metadata. No existing public API signatures should be removed or renamed.

behavior: The internal helper _get_keep_attrs is now called with default=True instead of default=False in all reduction, map, binary-op, where, isnull, notnull, quantile, coarsen_reshape, and apply_ufunc code paths.
Binary operations on Variable and Dataset now invoke merge_attrs with the drop_conflicts strategy to combine self.attrs and other.attrs, instead of unconditionally taking self.attrs.
Dataset.map now wraps non-DataArray return values into DataArray instances before further processing.
Dataset.map with keep_attrs=False now explicitly sets attrs to an empty dict on all result variables and coordinates, rather than relying on implicit behavior.
Docstrings for reduce methods on Variable, DataArray, and Dataset now document True as the default for keep_attrs.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray with attrs is reduced via mean(), sum(), std(), var(), min(), max(), median(), or quantile() without specifying keep_attrs, the result should carry the original attrs.
When two DataArrays with partially overlapping attrs are added, the result.attrs should contain only the key-value pairs that are identical in both operands; conflicting keys should be absent.
When a DataArray with attrs is combined with a scalar (e.g., data * 2), the result should preserve all of the DataArray's attrs.
When a Dataset with attrs is reduced via Dataset.reduce or Dataset.map without specifying keep_attrs, the result Dataset and its data variables should carry their original attrs.
When xr.set_options(keep_attrs=False) is active, all operations should drop attrs as they did prior to the upgrade.
When keep_attrs=False is passed explicitly to a reduction or binary operation, the result should have empty or no attrs regardless of the global setting.
When xr.where is called without specifying keep_attrs, attributes should be preserved on the result.
When apply_ufunc is called without specifying keep_attrs, the result should preserve attributes.
When isnull() or notnull() is called on a DataArray or Dataset without specifying keep_attrs, the result should preserve attributes.
Binary attribute merging should be order-independent: (a + b).attrs should equal (b + a).attrs when both operands carry attrs.

task_8.title: Fix ValueError when indexing lazy-loaded data with empty arrays in h5netcdf and scipy backends
task_8.description: When using the h5netcdf or scipy backends, indexing a lazy-loaded DataArray with an empty array (e.g., `.isel(dim_0=[])`) raised a ValueError because the outer indexer decomposition attempted to compute `np.max` and `np.min` on a zero-size array. The fix ensures that empty array keys are recognized early and converted to empty slices, so accessing `.values` on a zero-length selection returns an empty array as expected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that indexing a lazy-loaded DataArray or Dataset variable with an empty integer array (selecting zero elements) does not raise a ValueError when using the h5netcdf or scipy backends. Previously, performing an empty selection on data that had not yet been loaded into memory (e.g., via `.isel(dim_0=[])`) and then accessing `.values` caused a crash with 'zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity'. After the fix, this operation should return an empty NumPy array, consistent with the behavior of the netcdf4 engine and of eagerly-loaded data.

expectation.grounded: When `_decompose_outer_indexer` encounters an `np.ndarray` key with `size == 0` within `indexer_elems`, it must (1) treat the gain for that key as 0 rather than calling `np.max`/`np.min`, and (2) append `slice(0, 0)` to the backend indexer instead of computing a min/max-based slice. This ensures `explicit_indexing_adapter` produces a valid empty result for backends using `BackendIndexing` or `OuterIndexing` support, including `H5NetCDFArrayWrapper` and the scipy backend array wrapper. The final `.values` access must return a NumPy array with a zero-length dimension and no error.
expectation.conceptual: When a user selects zero elements from a lazy-loaded variable via integer-array indexing, the backend indexer decomposition should gracefully handle the empty selection and produce an empty result. Accessing `.values` on the resulting DataArray must return an empty NumPy array without raising any exception, regardless of the storage backend.

constraints.grounded: Non-empty array indexing behavior in `_decompose_outer_indexer` must remain unchanged: the gain calculation, the array-index selection via `np.argmax`, and the slice-based backend indexer construction for non-empty keys must produce identical results as before. The fix must not alter the code path for scalar, slice, or non-empty `np.ndarray` keys. The netcdf4 backend, which was not affected, must continue to work correctly.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must only address the empty-array edge case without regressing any existing indexing behavior. All backends that previously worked with non-empty selections must continue to produce identical results. Backends that already handled empty selections correctly (e.g., netcdf4) must remain unaffected.

behavior: When an np.ndarray indexer key has size 0, its gain value is computed as 0 instead of attempting np.max/np.min on the empty array.
When an np.ndarray indexer key has size 0, it is converted to slice(0, 0) in the backend indexer, yielding an empty slice selection.
Accessing .values on a lazy-loaded DataArray that has been sliced to zero elements via the h5netcdf backend now returns an empty NumPy array instead of raising ValueError.
Accessing .values on a lazy-loaded DataArray that has been sliced to zero elements via the scipy backend now returns an empty NumPy array instead of raising ValueError.
The behavior for eagerly-loaded data with empty selections remains unchanged (already returned empty arrays).
The behavior for non-empty array indexing remains unchanged across all backends.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray is opened with engine='h5netcdf' and indexed with an empty list (e.g., `.isel(dim_0=[])`), accessing `.values` should return an empty NumPy array with the appropriate shape.
When a DataArray is opened with engine='scipy' and indexed with an empty list, accessing `.values` should return an empty NumPy array with the appropriate shape.
Given a lazy-loaded DataArray with any backend, when indexed with a non-empty integer array, the result should be identical to the behavior before this fix.
Given a DataArray that is eagerly loaded (via `.load()`) and then indexed with an empty list, the result should be an empty array, consistent with pre-fix behavior.

When a multi-dimensional variable is indexed with a mix of empty and non-empty array indexers across different dimensions, the decomposition should handle the empty dimensions as empty slices and the non-empty dimensions normally.
No ValueError or other exception should be raised at any point during empty-array indexing of lazy-loaded data.

task_6.title: Fix h5netcdf backend format=None handling to match netcdf4 backend
task_6.description: The h5netcdf backend previously treated a None format value inconsistently compared to the netcdf4 backend. When format=None was passed (or defaulted), the h5netcdf backend left the internal format as None rather than resolving it to a concrete format string, causing inconsistent behavior. This fix aligns the h5netcdf backend with the netcdf4 backend by defaulting format to NETCDF4, properly propagating the resolved format through the store initialization, and additionally accepting NETCDF4_CLASSIC as a valid format option.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the h5netcdf backend resolves format=None to a concrete default format consistent with the netcdf4 backend. Previously, passing format=None (or relying on the default) left the internal format state as None, leading to inconsistent behavior between the two backends. The fix must also ensure that the NETCDF4_CLASSIC format is accepted by the h5netcdf backend and that the resolved format value is properly propagated through store construction.

expectation.grounded: When H5NetCDFStore.open() or H5netcdfBackendEntrypoint.open_dataset/open_datatree/open_groups is called with format=None or without specifying format, the format must resolve to 'NETCDF4'. The H5NetCDFStore instance's format attribute must reflect the resolved format string, never None. The backend must accept both 'NETCDF4' and 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC' as valid format values. Passing any other format string must raise a ValueError that includes the invalid format value. The resolved format must be propagated from the open() class method into the H5NetCDFStore constructor.
expectation.conceptual: When a user opens a dataset using the h5netcdf backend without specifying a format (or explicitly passing None), the backend should behave identically to the netcdf4 backend by defaulting to the NETCDF4 format. The backend should also support the NETCDF4_CLASSIC format. Invalid format values should be rejected with a clear error message indicating which value was invalid.

constraints.grounded: The H5NetCDFStore.format attribute must never be None after initialization; it must always hold a resolved format string. The set of accepted formats for the h5netcdf backend must be 'NETCDF4' and 'NETCDF4_CLASSIC'. The default format parameter across H5NetCDFStore.__init__, H5NetCDFStore.open, and H5netcdfBackendEntrypoint entry points must be 'NETCDF4'. The ValueError raised for invalid formats must include the rejected format value in the message.
constraints.conceptual: The h5netcdf backend must never operate with an undefined or null format state. Its format handling rules must be consistent with the netcdf4 backend. Existing workflows that previously relied on the default format=None must continue to work without modification, as the resolved behavior is equivalent.

behavior: When format=None is passed to the h5netcdf backend, it resolves to 'NETCDF4' instead of remaining None.
The default value of the format parameter in all h5netcdf backend entry points changes from None to 'NETCDF4'.

The H5NetCDFStore.format attribute is always a concrete string after initialization, never None.

The resolved format is properly propagated from the open() class method to the H5NetCDFStore constructor.

The h5netcdf backend's default format behavior should be consistent with the netcdf4 backend's default format behavior.

task_9.title: Fix error handling in decode_cf_variables to preserve original exception
task_9.description: The decode_cf_variables function previously attempted to re-raise caught exceptions by constructing a new instance of the same exception type with a single string argument. This broke for exception types whose constructors require additional positional arguments (e.g., aiohttp.client_exceptions.ClientResponseError), producing a secondary TypeError that masked the original error and prevented callers from catching it properly. The fix replaces the faulty re-construction pattern with Python's exception note mechanism (add_note) and a bare re-raise, preserving the original exception type, message, and traceback while still annotating it with the variable name that caused the failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when an exception occurs during CF variable decoding in decode_cf_variables, the original exception is propagated to callers with its original type and traceback intact, annotated with context about which variable triggered the failure. Previously, the function attempted to construct a new exception of the caught type using a single-string-argument constructor call, which caused a TypeError for exception classes with non-standard constructors (e.g., those requiring additional positional arguments), masking the real error and preventing proper upstream error handling.

expectation.grounded: When decode_cf_variables catches an Exception during variable decoding, it must call add_note on the caught exception to annotate it with the variable name context, then re-raise the original exception unchanged. The re-raised exception must retain its original type, so that callers filtering by specific exception classes (e.g., ClientResponseError, KeyError, ValueError) can still catch it. No new exception instance of type(e) should be constructed.
expectation.conceptual: When variable decoding fails inside decode_cf_variables, the original exception must propagate to the caller with its original type and traceback preserved. Additional context about which variable caused the failure should be attached as a note on the exception rather than by constructing a new exception object. Callers must be able to catch the exception by its original type without encountering a secondary TypeError.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter the exception type that propagates from decode_cf_variables — any except clause upstream that matched the original exception type must continue to match. The annotation must include the variable name that triggered the error. The function must not swallow or wrap the exception in a different type. The original traceback chain must be preserved.
constraints.conceptual: Error propagation from CF variable decoding must be transparent to upstream exception handlers. The original error identity and type must never be altered. Contextual information about the failing variable should be additive metadata, not a replacement of the original error.

behavior: When an exception of any type is raised during CF variable decoding, decode_cf_variables now re-raises the exact same exception object instead of constructing a new instance of the exception's type.
A note is added to the caught exception via add_note indicating which variable was being decoded when the error occurred, including the variable name and its representation.
Exception types with non-standard constructors (e.g., those requiring positional arguments beyond a message string) no longer cause a secondary TypeError during error handling.
The original exception's type, message, attributes, and traceback are fully preserved, allowing upstream callers to catch specific exception types as expected.
The previous behavior of chaining via 'from e' is replaced by a bare re-raise, so the exception's __cause__ is no longer set; instead the original exception propagates directly.
acceptance_criteria: When decode_cf_variables encounters an exception during decoding of a variable, the exception that propagates to the caller must be of the same type as the original exception.

When an exception with a non-standard constructor (requiring positional arguments beyond a single message string) is raised during variable decoding, no secondary TypeError should occur — the original exception must propagate cleanly.
When a decoding error is raised and caught by a caller, the exception object must contain a note referencing the name of the variable that caused the failure.
When catching a decoding error, the exception's original message, attributes, and traceback must be intact and unmodified apart from the added note.

task_10.title: Fix equivalent() for NumPy scalar NaN comparison in attribute merging
task_10.description: The equivalent() utility function failed to recognize two NumPy scalar NaN values as equivalent, because np.float64(np.nan) == np.float64(np.nan) returns np.bool_(False) rather than Python bool False. The old code path converted this non-bool result to Python bool and returned False immediately, skipping the NaN equivalence check entirely. This caused attribute-merging operations such as combine_attrs='drop_conflicts' to incorrectly drop NaN-valued attributes after a NetCDF roundtrip, where Python float NaN values are deserialized as NumPy scalar NaN values. The fix reorders the NaN equivalence check to occur before the equality comparison, ensuring both Python float NaN and NumPy scalar NaN are handled correctly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the equivalent() function correctly identifies two NaN-valued attributes as equivalent regardless of whether they are Python float NaN or NumPy scalar NaN. Previously, after saving a DataArray to NetCDF and reloading it, NaN attributes (e.g., fill_value: np.nan) were silently dropped during concat or merge operations that use combine_attrs='drop_conflicts', because the NaN equivalence check was bypassed for NumPy scalar types.

expectation.grounded: The equivalent() function must return True when both arguments are NaN, including when they are np.float64(np.nan) or other NumPy floating-point scalar NaN types. The pd.isnull() check must be evaluated before the equality comparison so that np.bool_ results from NumPy scalar equality never short-circuit the NaN detection. When combine_attrs='drop_conflicts' is used with xr.concat or xr.merge, attributes whose values are NaN (in any scalar representation) must be preserved as matching rather than dropped as conflicting.
expectation.conceptual: The equivalence check for attribute values must treat NaN as equal to NaN in all common scalar representations. Attribute-merging strategies that rely on equivalence (such as drop_conflicts) must preserve NaN-valued attributes that match across inputs, even after serialization roundtrips that may change the NaN representation from Python float to NumPy scalar.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter the behavior of equivalent() for non-NaN values, arrays, lists, or Dataset/Series types. The list_equiv delegation path must remain unchanged. The function must still return False when comparing NaN against a non-NaN value. The pd.isnull() call must handle types where pd.isnull raises or returns non-boolean by not regressing the existing guard logic for non-boolean equality results.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be limited to fixing NaN-vs-NaN equivalence for scalar values. All other equivalence semantics—including array equivalence, list equivalence, and rejection of non-boolean comparison results—must remain unaffected. Non-NaN attribute comparisons must continue to work identically.

behavior: equivalent(np.float64(np.nan), np.float64(np.nan)) now returns True instead of False
equivalent(float('nan'), float('nan')) continues to return True
equivalent(np.float32(np.nan), np.float32(np.nan)) now returns True instead of False
equivalent(np.nan, np.float64(np.nan)) now returns True for cross-type NaN comparison
NaN-valued attributes are preserved through xr.concat with combine_attrs='drop_conflicts' after NetCDF roundtrip
equivalent() still returns False for NaN vs non-NaN comparisons
equivalent() still returns True for equal non-NaN scalar values
equivalent() behavior for arrays, lists, and non-scalar types is unchanged

When equivalent() is called with two Python float('nan') values, it should return True
When equivalent() is called with mixed NaN types (e.g., float('nan') and np.float64(np.nan)), it should return True
When two DataArrays with fill_value=np.nan attributes are saved to NetCDF, reloaded, and concatenated with combine_attrs='drop_conflicts', the fill_value attribute should be preserved in the result
When equivalent() is called with np.float64(np.nan) and a non-NaN value, it should return False
When equivalent() is called with two equal non-NaN scalars, it should return True
When equivalent() is called with two non-equal non-NaN scalars, it should return False
When equivalent() is called with list or array arguments, behavior should be unchanged from prior version

task_7.title: Stricter backend URL detection to prevent incorrect remote URL claiming
task_7.description: Previously, when multiple I/O backends (netcdf4, h5netcdf, pydap, scipy) were installed, the backend resolution mechanism would greedily claim any remote URL, causing backends like pydap or netcdf4 to incorrectly intercept remote Zarr stores and other non-DAP/non-netCDF URLs. This change makes each backend's guess_can_open method stricter: the netcdf4 backend now only claims remote URLs with netCDF file extensions; the pydap backend only claims URLs with explicit DAP protocol indicators; the h5netcdf backend no longer attempts to read magic numbers from remote URIs; and the scipy backend explicitly refuses remote URIs. Additionally, the is_remote_uri utility now supports uppercase URI scheme letters, a new strip_uri_params utility correctly handles URLs containing query parameters or fragments when checking extensions, and the scipy backend's extension matching was corrected to support compound .nc.gz suffixes while dropping the incorrect standalone .nc4 extension claim.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray's automatic backend selection no longer incorrectly routes remote URLs to the netcdf4 or pydap backends when the URL does not point to a netCDF or DAP resource. Previously, opening a remote Zarr store (or any non-DAP, non-netCDF URL) without an explicit engine= argument could silently select the wrong backend if netcdf4 or pydap was installed, leading to confusing errors or incorrect data reads. Each backend's guess_can_open method must apply protocol-aware and extension-aware heuristics so that only genuinely compatible URLs are claimed.

expectation.grounded: NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must return True for remote URIs only when the URL (after stripping query parameters and fragments via strip_uri_params) has a netCDF extension (.nc, .nc4, .cdf); it must return False for all other remote URLs. PydapBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must return True only for URLs using dap2:// or dap4:// schemes, or remote URIs containing /dap2/, /dap4/, or /dodsC/ path segments; it must return False for all other inputs including generic http(s) URLs. H5netcdfBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must skip magic number reading for remote URIs (detected via is_remote_uri) and only perform magic number checks on local files. ScipyBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must return False for any remote URI. The is_remote_uri utility must recognize URI schemes with uppercase letters (e.g., HTTP://, S3://). ScipyBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must recognize compound extensions like .nc.gz using Path.suffixes and must no longer match the standalone .nc4 extension.
expectation.conceptual: When xarray opens a dataset from a URL without an explicit engine argument, each backend should only volunteer to handle URLs that match its supported protocol and file type. The netcdf4 backend should claim remote URLs only if they have a netCDF file extension. The pydap backend should claim remote URLs only if they carry explicit DAP protocol markers. The h5netcdf and scipy backends should not claim remote URLs at all. URI scheme detection should be case-insensitive. Extension detection for remote URLs should correctly ignore query parameters and URL fragments.

constraints.grounded: NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must still return True for local files that have a valid netCDF magic number (CDF or HDF5 signature) or a .nc/.nc4/.cdf extension. NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint must still handle bytes and memoryview inputs via magic number check. H5netcdfBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must still correctly identify local HDF5 files by magic number. ScipyBackendEntrypoint must still correctly identify local .nc, .cdf, and .nc.gz files (including gzip-compressed files via magic number). PydapBackendEntrypoint must continue to accept URLs with /dodsC/ path segments (THREDDS OPeNDAP convention). Existing workflows that pass engine= explicitly must remain unaffected regardless of URL pattern.
constraints.conceptual: All existing local file opening workflows must continue to work unchanged. Backends must not break when the user explicitly specifies the engine argument, even for URLs that the backend would no longer auto-detect. The fix must not prevent any backend from opening resources it is genuinely capable of handling; it only restricts automatic selection heuristics.

task_12.title: Fix drop_sel on MultiIndex with mixed-type levels
task_12.description: drop_sel raised a KeyError when called on a MultiIndex whose levels contain mixed types (e.g., str and int), even though sel handled the same selection correctly. The root cause was an unconditional np.asarray conversion of the label arguments inside Dataset.drop_sel, which coerced all elements to a single dtype and corrupted the lookup keys. The fix restricts that array conversion to the special case of DataArray labels and otherwise passes labels through unmodified, letting the underlying pandas indexer handle type-appropriate conversion.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.drop_sel and DataArray.drop_sel work correctly on MultiIndex coordinates whose levels have heterogeneous types (e.g., a MultiIndex stacked from a string dimension and an integer dimension). Previously, calling drop_sel with a tuple key on such a MultiIndex raised a KeyError because label types were silently coerced, while the equivalent sel call succeeded.

expectation.grounded: When drop_sel is called on a Dataset or DataArray with a MultiIndex whose levels have different dtypes, the method should resolve the label without raising a KeyError. The labels passed to the pandas Index.drop or MultiIndex.drop path must preserve their original per-level types. The only case where labels should be eagerly converted via np.asarray is when the caller passes a DataArray as labels. For all other label types (tuples, lists, scalars), conversion responsibility is deferred to the pandas indexer.
expectation.conceptual: drop_sel should behave consistently with sel when operating on MultiIndex coordinates. Selecting and dropping by the same key on the same MultiIndex should both succeed without type-related errors. Label types should be preserved through the drop_sel pipeline so that mixed-type MultiIndex lookups resolve correctly.

constraints.grounded: DataArray-typed labels must still be converted to a numpy array before being passed to the indexer, since pandas does not natively handle DataArray inputs. Scalar labels must still be wrapped in a list before the drop call. Existing behavior for single-type indexes (both regular Index and MultiIndex with uniform-type levels) must not regress. The errors parameter ('raise' or 'ignore') must continue to function as before.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not break any existing drop_sel usage on regular indexes or uniform-type MultiIndexes. The special handling for DataArray inputs must be preserved. Error handling semantics for missing labels must remain unchanged.

task_14.title: Optimize multi-dimension coarsening padding to a single pad operation
task_14.description: When coarsening along multiple dimensions with boundary='pad', xarray previously applied padding one dimension at a time inside a loop, creating intermediate arrays for each dimension. This caused unnecessary memory allocations and slower execution. The change accumulates all per-dimension pad widths and applies them in a single pad call after the loop, and also skips dimensions where the computed pad is zero. Benchmarks show 15–29% speed improvement and 15–18% memory reduction for multi-dimensional coarsening operations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that coarsening a DataArray or Dataset along multiple dimensions with boundary='pad' performs padding efficiently in a single operation rather than serially per dimension. The optimization must reduce peak memory usage and execution time without altering the numerical result of the coarsen operation.

expectation.grounded: When Variable.coarsen_reshape is called with multiple dimensions and boundary='pad', all required pad widths should be collected and passed to Variable.pad in a single invocation. If a dimension's computed pad width is zero, it should be skipped entirely. The method must still raise TypeError for invalid boundary values and correctly handle 'trim', 'exact', and 'pad' boundaries. The final reshaped output must be numerically identical to the previous serial-padding implementation.
expectation.conceptual: Multi-dimension coarsening with pad boundary should consolidate all padding into one operation instead of applying padding separately for each dimension. Dimensions that need no padding should be skipped. The coarsened result must remain numerically identical to the prior behavior.

constraints.grounded: The coarsen_reshape method must still support all three boundary modes ('exact', 'trim', 'pad') and raise TypeError for invalid boundary values. Padding with side='left' must place zeros before the data, and side='right' must place zeros after the data, consistent with prior semantics. Single-dimension coarsening must continue to work correctly. The pad call must use mode='constant'.
constraints.conceptual: All existing boundary modes and side configurations must continue to produce identical results. Single-dimension coarsening must not regress. No change in the public API or observable output beyond improved performance.

behavior: When coarsening along N dimensions with boundary='pad', only a single pad operation is performed instead of N separate pad operations.
When a dimension's size is already an exact multiple of the coarsening window, no padding is computed for that dimension and it is skipped.

task_11.title: Restore Dataset.map() support for non-DataArray outputs and revise keep_attrs default
task_11.description: Dataset.map() regressed after an internal refactor (PR #10602), raising AttributeError when the mapping function returned non-DataArray values such as scalars or numpy arrays. This fix restores backward compatibility by converting non-DataArray return values to DataArray objects. Additionally, the default value of keep_attrs was changed from False to True, meaning attributes are now preserved by default, and explicit attribute clearing was added when keep_attrs is False.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.map() correctly handles mapping functions that return non-DataArray values (e.g., scalars, numpy arrays, or mixed DataArray/non-DataArray outputs) without raising AttributeError. Ensure that the keep_attrs parameter defaults to True so that variable and coordinate attributes are preserved by default. Ensure that when keep_attrs is explicitly set to False, all attributes on variables and coordinates are explicitly cleared.

expectation.grounded: When Dataset.map() receives a function that returns a non-DataArray value (scalar, numpy array, etc.), the result should be automatically wrapped into a DataArray via the DataArray constructor before coordinate merging. The keep_attrs parameter should default to True (via _get_keep_attrs with default=True), causing variable and coordinate attributes to be copied from the source Dataset by default. When keep_attrs is False, the attrs dict on all result variables and coordinates should be explicitly set to empty. The method should return a valid Dataset in all cases.
expectation.conceptual: Dataset.map() should accept any mapping function regardless of whether it returns DataArray objects or plain values. Attributes should be preserved by default, and explicitly stripped when the user opts out of attribute preservation. The method should never raise internal errors due to unexpected return types from the user-supplied function.

constraints.grounded: Existing Dataset.map() calls that return DataArray values must continue to work identically. The conversion to DataArray for non-DataArray outputs must use the DataArray constructor without injecting extra dimensions or coordinates. The coordinate merging via merge_coordinates_without_align must still operate on DataArray.coords. When keep_attrs is True, attribute copying for coordinates must only apply to coordinates that exist in the source Dataset's coords.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter behavior for existing usage patterns where the mapping function returns DataArray objects. Attribute handling must be deterministic: either all attributes are preserved or all are cleared, with no partial or inconsistent state. The change must not introduce new coordinate alignment or dimension inference side effects.

task_13.title: Optimize xarray.concat() memory usage and speed
task_13.description: The xarray.concat() function exhibited excessive peak memory usage (up to 6x the size of inputs) and was significantly slower than the underlying np.concatenate (up to 5x slower). This was caused by the allocation of large intermediate index arrays and the use of expensive pandas-based reindexing during concatenation. The optimization eliminates unnecessary large array allocations, replaces pandas-based index lookup with an efficient cumulative-sum approach for the reindexer, and lazily allocates a single reusable reindexer buffer. The result is roughly 5x lower peak memory and 10x faster execution for large concatenation workloads.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray.concat() does not allocate large intermediate index arrays proportional to the total concatenation size. Previously, concatenating DataArrays or Datasets along a dimension caused peak memory usage far exceeding the combined size of inputs and output (reported as 6x input size), and wall-clock time several times slower than np.concatenate, even with large chunk sizes and no coordinates or indexes requiring special treatment. The overhead should be minimized so that memory and time costs scale proportionally to the actual data size, not to redundant internal bookkeeping.

expectation.grounded: xarray.concat() must avoid creating a full-range np.arange index array over the concatenation dimension length. The concat_index_size should be derived directly from the cumulative dimension lengths rather than from a materialized index array. When variables are missing from some datasets and reindexing is required, the reindexer array must be allocated at most once (lazily) and reused across loop iterations. The reindexer must be computed via np.cumsum on the boolean variable_index_mask rather than through pd.Index.get_indexer. The reindexer must use a minimal signed integer dtype (via np.min_scalar_type) that can represent -1 as a sentinel for missing positions. The check for whether reindexing is needed must use variable_index_mask.all() instead of comparing lengths of a materialized sub-index.
expectation.conceptual: xarray.concat() should exhibit peak memory usage and execution time that scale proportionally to the combined size of the input data and output result, without large intermediate allocations. When some variables are absent from certain input datasets and reindexing is required, the internal reindexing mechanism should use a single reusable buffer with an efficient computation strategy rather than repeatedly constructing and querying index objects.

constraints.grounded: The reindexing behavior must remain correct: positions where a variable is present must map to consecutive zero-based indices, and positions where it is absent must be filled according to the fill_value parameter. The variable_reindexer must use -1 as the sentinel value for missing positions. The concat result must be identical to the previous version for all inputs, including cases with missing variables, mixed dtypes, coordinates, and indexes. No regression in correctness for edge cases such as concatenating zero-length arrays, single-element lists, or datasets with partially overlapping variables.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must not change the observable output of xarray.concat() for any valid input. All existing fill-value and reindexing semantics must be preserved. Memory and performance improvements must not introduce correctness regressions for any combination of input datasets, dimensions, coordinates, or fill values.

behavior: xarray.concat() no longer materializes a full np.arange array spanning the total concatenation dimension length, eliminating a major source of unnecessary memory allocation.
The concat_index_size is computed directly from cumulative dimension lengths without creating an intermediate array.

A variable_reindexer buffer is lazily allocated only when reindexing is actually needed (i.e., when a variable is not present in all datasets), and is reused across all variables requiring reindexing within the same concat call.
The reindexer is computed via np.cumsum on a boolean mask and adjusted to use zero-based indexing with -1 sentinels for missing positions, replacing the previous pd.Index.get_indexer approach.
The check for whether reindexing is needed uses variable_index_mask.all() instead of comparing lengths of materialized index arrays.
The reindexer uses a minimal signed integer dtype determined by np.min_scalar_type to minimize memory footprint.
Peak memory usage is reduced by approximately 5x and execution time by approximately 10x for large 1D concatenation workloads.
acceptance_criteria: When concatenating 10 DataArrays of 100 MiB each along a single dimension with no coordinates, peak memory usage during xarray.concat() should not exceed approximately 2x the combined input size (previously was ~6x).
When concatenating large DataArrays along a single dimension, xarray.concat() wall-clock time should be within a small constant factor of np.concatenate for the same data, not 5x or more slower.

When concatenating datasets where some variables are absent from certain inputs, the resulting dataset must contain those variables with fill_value in the positions corresponding to the datasets where they were missing, identical to the behavior before the optimization.
When concatenating datasets with all variables present in all inputs, no reindexer buffer should be allocated (lazy allocation).
When concatenating datasets with partially overlapping variables, the reindexer buffer should be allocated exactly once and reused for all variables requiring reindexing.
The result of xarray.concat() must be bitwise identical to the pre-optimization result for all valid inputs, including edge cases with mixed dtypes, empty arrays, and complex coordinate structures.
